title: Python desync: no GUARD_PPM drift-desync transition (decision guard-ppm)
description: DIVERGENT (contradicts final decision guard-ppm whose rationale says all implementations use 5000). Req 2a.6.2: 'SYNCED + Excessive clock drift (drift_ppm > GUARD_PPM) -> DESYNCED, trigger epoch_floor revalidation'; GUARD_PPM=5000. Evidence: python/src/lichen/timing/sfn.py DesyncFSM (:77-133) has no drift input; python/src/lichen/sim/tdma.py:119-124 apply_drift computes drift but nothing compares it to 5000 ppm; DESYNC_CONSTANTS (sfn.py:60-65) lack GUARD_PPM. C and Rust implement drift->DESYNCED (C desync_fsm test consumes ccp16-desync.json 12000>5000 ppm case, link.h:656 5000U; Rust lichen-link/src/tdma_clock.rs:83-85 holdover_expired + ccp7_holdover.json vectors). Fix: add GUARD_PPM=5000 constant + drift transition to Python DesyncFSM and a drift-desync vector consumer. Suggested placement: python/src/lichen/timing/sfn.py + tests/test_ccp_sync_vector_consumers.py.
close_reason: Python drift-desync gate landed per 2a.6.2 / decision guard-ppm (GUARD_PPM=5000): (1) DESYNC_CONSTANTS gained GUARD_PPM=5000 with a comment citing C LICHEN_DRIFT_MAX_HOLDOVER_PPM (5000U, link.h:656) and Rust holdover_expired (lichen-link tdma_clock.rs); (2) new module-level holdover_expired(measured_drift_ppm, guard_ppm=5000) — abs(drift) > guard, matching Rust unsigned_abs() > guard_ppm parity; (3) DesyncFSM.on_drift(drift_ppm) — stays SYNCED when |drift| <= 5000 (strictly-greater semantics, exactly-5000 stays), transitions DESYNCED with counter reset when strictly above; application from RECOVERING is fail-closed. Tests: drift boundary (4000/5000/12000 per the ccp16-desync.json 12000>5000 case), counter reset, holdover_expired parity (positive/negative/exact boundary). Verification: 89/89 sfn tests, 192/192 sfn+desync-scoped suite, ruff clean. Codereview (Kimi K3): PASS, no findings; reviewer notes spec 2a.6.3 table still lists GUARD_PPM 250 — the 5000 decision hasn't propagated to the spec table (spec-sync tracked by the b7z9 family sweep owner; the Rust/C implementations and this Python gate all follow the 5000 decision).
